name: The Volatile Tabernacle

detectability.signature: Paired annihilation gamma spikes at the 511 keV line flashing across the pocket in migrating chains; a gravimetric shadow with no baryonic source

proximity: Gamma flux rises steeply with each closing light-second
Sensors track annihilation flashes crawling across the pocket's interior in braided chains
contact: Shield contact with confined antimatter triggers localized annihilation storms
Magnetic confinement filaments lash out and erode hull surfaces on touch
prolonged_exposure: Cumulative radiation load overwhelms shielding and crew alike within hours
Any confinement breach escalates within seconds to civilization-ending yield

phenomena: Unusual gravitational readings despite minimal baryonic mass
hazards: Molecular disintegration in any confinement collapse
opportunities: Exotic matter collection of antihydrogen and rarer isotopes
Unique research opportunity into baryon asymmetry
known_incidents: The harvester Ambitious Measure clipped a confinement filament in 2387; the resulting flash was logged as a supernova in two neighboring sectors
Automated collection drones return valuable antihydrogen roughly once in forty launches
description: The Volatile Tabernacle is a sixty-thousand-kilometer vault of magnetically confined antimatter, veiled in braided filaments of force and lit from within by ceaseless annihilation. Gamma flashes at the characteristic 511 keV line ripple across its face in migrating chains, lending the sphere the look of a shrine lamp seen through stained glass. Gravimetrically it registers far heavier than its faint baryonic signature should ever allow.

The confinement is failing by increments, and the pocket contracts year over year as ordinary matter leaks inward to meet its twin. Filaments lash unpredictably at anything conductive drifting near, and harvest drones survive only through luck dressed as engineering. There is no cycle to the violence, only worsening odds.

System records suggest the pocket condensed from primordial asymmetry remnants over two billion years ago, a leftover altar where creation's ledger never quite balanced. The Ambitious Measure disaster, misread as a supernova from two sectors away, rewrote regional insurance law overnight. Antimatter cartels nonetheless circle it like moths carrying ledgers.

An exclusion sphere forty million kilometers wide is enforced by warning buoys replaced, on average, annually. Researchers monitor the contraction continuously, and their best models differ only on whether the end arrives in millennia or on a Tuesday. Should the Tabernacle ever fully fail, the resulting flash will be somebody's final data point.
